decisions.question: ADR-002 says plugin rules report at INFO; nidana-checks@v1 G1 declares three rules at WARNING and one at INFO. Which of the two is wrong?

options.label: ADR-002 is wrong, correct it in place
options.consequence: ADR-002's Context and Consequences state the mechanism; nidana-checks@v1, its G1 and its seventeen recorded invocations stay as they are

options.label: nidana-checks@v1 is wrong, report a run-stop-candidate
options.consequence: G1 and the analyze-* recorded invocations would need a breaking change; nidana.tooling.lint could not phase-plan until it is settled

decisions.chosen: ADR-002 is wrong, correct it in place
decisions.why: The experiment reproduces both observations with one probe plugin on the pinned analyzer 13.3.0 and analysis_server_plugin 0.3.18. A diagnostic reports at the severity the plugin's diagnostics section configures for its code, otherwise at the severity its LintCode declares; LintCode's constructor defaults that to INFO. registerWarningRule versus registerLintRule decides only default enablement, and the reported type is always STATIC_WARNING. The workspace-layout stand-ins construct LintCode with no severity (hence INFO); the nidana-checks-fixtures stand-in passes severity: DiagnosticSeverity.WARNING for three codes and nothing for unflagged_sensitive_topic (hence WARNING and INFO). So ADR-002 generalized a property of its stand-in into a property of plugins. nidana-checks@v1 G1 is achievable as written and agrees with the observed exit codes (C3: INFO exits 0, 1 under --fatal-infos; C4: WARNING exits 2; C5: ERROR exits 3). The blast radius is the ADR's text only: no contract, interface or node changes.

experiments.question: On analyzer 13.3.0 and analysis_server_plugin 0.3.18, what decides the severity at which a plugin diagnostic reports under fvm dart analyze, and why did workspace-layout see INFO where nidana-checks-fixtures saw WARNING?
experiments.finding: The severity configured for the code in the plugin's diagnostics section wins; otherwise the LintCode's declared severity, which defaults to INFO. registerWarningRule versus registerLintRule decides only default enablement (warning rules run unless disabled, lint rules only when enabled, also by a configured severity). The type is STATIC_WARNING for all. Exit codes: ERROR 3, WARNING 2, INFO 0 or 1 under --fatal-infos. workspace-layout's stand-ins declare no severity; nidana-checks-fixtures' declares WARNING on three codes. Both experiments were right about their stand-ins; nidana-checks@v1 is consistent.
